answer: A perishable-bond registry is one workable check. Each new agent identity escrows a lot of saffron whose farm and harvest week sit in a public provenance atlas. The bond is a dated physical claim that decays: it counts only while the spice is near the zenith of its aroma, confirmed by a random taster cracking the seal. A lot fades in months, so bonds cannot be recycled, and each fake persona needs its own farm record plus fresh tasting labour. An attacker renting a thousand identities must buy a thousand real lots and keep paying tasters, a linear cost that leaves a paper trail.
